scope: Mouse-wheel page navigation in vertical scrolls and parchment; development alpha

behavior.direction: Normalized wheel up selects the previous page; down selects the next page, independently of the pointer half
behavior.precision: One page per whole notch; fractional movement accumulates within the document and resets on close
behavior.routing: Wheel position and vertical delta enter the native event path; only the top modal vertical document receives navigation, excluding its close control and outside positions
behavior.bounds: Existing page handlers clamp at the first and last pages; each event performs at most the maximum document page count
behavior.interfaces: Internal event type and delta field, private document wheel handler and state; no external API, preference or CLI option

wheel_translation: Positive, negative, fractional, multi-notch and zero vertical deltas
Horizontal input stays outside vertical navigation
Wheel coordinates in fullscreen, 640 x 480 window and 1280 x 720 letterboxed window

layouts: pre-game Options variant invoked by harness
integration_scenarios.text: Original credits script 110 is rendered in both vertical document appearances to provide multiple original-data pages
checks: Wheel-rendered pages match existing arrow-key and mouse-click navigation byte-for-byte
Quarter/quarter/half-notch movement reaches exactly the next page
A two-notch movement matches two arrow-key page changes
Flipped-direction events navigate forward and backward correctly
Outside, close-control and horizontal-only input leave the page and fractional accumulation unchanged
Large wheel movements clamp at the first and last pages; opposite input leaves the boundary normally
Closing with a partial notch pending and reopening starts a fresh accumulator
Cursor pixels, hotspots, modal focus, actor position, party flags and settings remain correct
Books/Credits, Options and Hot Keys ignore wheel input
Prior save/load, Hot Keys, Credits content, keypad, music and speech regressions pass
integration_scenarios.ambient_audio: The longer document scenarios allow existing timed ambient sound selection to advance RNG. RNG is not asserted frozen across a long read; original timing and ambient behavior are preserved. Reference RNG checkpoints before the added UI scenarios remain identical.

memory.environment: Executed outside the sandbox to permit LeakSanitizer thread inspection

windows.build: Zig cross-build, Windows x64 Release, SDL 3.4.18
windows.execution: Native Windows processes from a preflight complete ZIP, with bundled-data discovery and an unrelated working directory

packages.validation: Final archives retain the executable and SDL library tested in the preflight package; the complete-package allowlist remains eight baseline-matching files

limitations: Automated SDL input; no new manual mouse-wheel or trackpad hardware test
